### Observed differences

- The direct successors of the cycle activities flipped. Earlier, about 94 in 100 of A01's outgoing transitions went to A07 (the rest mostly to A03 and A04); in the later window none went to A07, about 57 in 100 went to A05, and the remainder split across A06, A04 and A03 [DIR001]. Earlier, about 96 in 100 of A05's outgoing transitions returned to A01; later, about 91 in 100 go to A07 [DIR004]. Earlier, A07's outgoing transitions split between A05 (about 43 in 100) and A06 (about 41 in 100); later, about 94 in 100 go back to A01 [DIR006].
- Immediate succession changed accordingly: the distance-1 pairs A01→A07, A05→A01 and A07→A05 (each roughly a quarter to a third of observed pairs at distance 1 earlier) were not observed at distance 1 in the later window, while A01→A05, A05→A07 and A07→A01 became the dominant distance-1 pairs there (about 20–25 in 100 of observed pairs) [LAG003, LAG009, LAG013, LAG001, LAG011, LAG012].
- A05 and A07 now occur later within traces: A05's mean relative position rose from about 0.47 to 0.57 and A07's from about 0.51 to 0.69 [POS002, POS004]. A06 moved from the very end of traces (mean about 0.96) to the middle (about 0.48) [POS003].
- Participation moved in opposite directions: A01 appears in about 53 in 100 traces in the later window versus about 28 in 100 earlier (mean occurrences per trace about 1.10 versus 0.53), while A07 appears in about 29 in 100 versus about 51 in 100 earlier (mean about 0.57 versus 1.03) [OCC001, OCC002].
- Couplings changed: A03 and A04, which earlier always co-occurred with A07 (together in about 50 in 100 traces, never alone), now appear without A07 in about 24 in 100 traces [REL006, REL007]; A01 and A07, earlier together in about 28 in 100 traces with A07 alone in another 23, are now together in 29 with A01 alone in 24 [REL005]. A03 and A04 also now often lead directly back to A01 (about 34–39 in 100 of their outgoing transitions), which was rare earlier [DIR002, DIR003, LAG004, LAG006].
- A06's outgoing transitions, of which only about 11 were observed earlier (mostly to A03), rose to about 83 in the later window, spread over A01, A03, A05 and A04; the earlier side of this comparison rests on few observations [DIR005].

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the execution order of A05 and A07 within the repeating cycle around A01 was reversed: in the earlier window the cycle ran A01 → A07 → A05 → back to A01 (with A07 often passing to A06), while in the later window it runs A01 → A05 → A07 → back to A01 [DIR001, DIR004, DIR006, LAG001, LAG003, LAG009, LAG011, LAG012, LAG013]. The successor profiles of all three activities changed exactly as this re-sequencing predicts, the old distance-1 pairs disappeared while the new ones appeared, and the later positions of A05 and A07 fit; with 35 qualifying control-flow items against roughly 0.29 expected if nothing had changed, chance cannot account for the ensemble as a whole [DIR001, DIR004, DIR006, POS002, POS004]. Limitations: POS and LAG use event positions, so the hypothesis concerns sequence order rather than clock timing, and the evidence cannot rule out a broader rewiring beyond a two-activity exchange, since A01 simultaneously gained direct transitions to A03, A04 and A06 and the participation of A01 and A07 shifted [DIR001, OCC001, OCC002].

Other differences: A06 moved from the end of traces to the middle and now branches to several successors instead of mainly A03, though the earlier profile rests on about 11 outgoing transitions and some later pair observations are also sparse [POS003, DIR005]. A03 and A04 decoupled from A07, and A01 and A07 now often occur in separate traces [REL005, REL006, REL007].

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

Screening: 58 units tested, 35 items qualified, 0.29 expected without change. 35 items is vastly more than 0.29 expected — this is a massive excess, so chance cannot explain the whole set. So we're beyond "insufficient evidence" by the screening comparison. Now judge by directness, consistency, and ability to rule out competing explanations.

All evidence is control-flow family (OCC, DIR, POS, REL, LAG). No time (TWAIT) or resource items, so I must not discuss time or resources.

Let me reconstruct the behaviour.

OCC001: A01 — before: mean 0.525/trace, participation 27.5% (55/200 traces), recurrence 0.11. After: mean 1.095, participation 53% (106/200), recurrence 0.29. So A01 roughly doubled in participation and mean occurrences.

OCC002: A07 — before: mean 1.03, participation 50.5% (101/200), recurrence 0.275. After: mean 0.565, participation 29% (58/200), recurrence 0.14. A07 roughly halved.

DIR001 (A01's outgoing): before, A01 → A07 in ~94% of A01's outgoing transitions (0.9429), tiny shares to A03 (0.038) and A04 (0.019). After: A01 → A05 0.574, A06 0.182, A04 0.135, A03 0.108; A07 gone (0). So after, A01 leads to A05 mostly, plus A06/A04/A03; before it led almost exclusively to A07.

DIR004 (A05's outgoing): before, A05 → A01 0.962. After: A05 → A07 0.912, A06 0.062. So before A05 was followed by A01; after A05 is followed by A07.

DIR006 (A07's outgoing): before, A07 → A05 0.432, A06 0.413, A03 0.073, A04 0.083 (support 206 outgoing transitions — A07 occurred a lot before). After: A07 → A01 0.938 (support 113). So after, A07 leads almost exclusively to A01.

So we have a cycle: A01 → A07 → A01 in the after window? A01 → A05 → A07 → A01? Let's check: after, A01 → A05 (57%), A05 → A07 (91%), A07 → A01 (94%). So a loop A01 → A05 → A07 → A01 in the after window. Before: A01 → A07 (94%), A07 → A05 (43%)/A06 (41%), A05 → A01 (96%). So before there was a loop A01 → A07 → A05 → A01 (and A07 → A06 → ...). Let's check A06: DIR005 (A06's outgoing): before: A06 → A03 0.636, A04 0.364 (support 11 — few observations). After: A06 → A01 0.313, A03 0.277, A04 0.145, A05 0.181, A07 0.084 (support 83). So A06 occurred rarely before (11 outgoing transitions) and more often after.

POS003 (A06): before mean position 0.964 (near end), after mean 0.479 (middle). So A06 moved from near the end of traces to the middle. Hmm, but POS uses positions not clock time; a position shift alone doesn't show the activity was moved. But combined with DIR it's consistent.

POS001 (A01): before mean 0.581, after 0.615, q75 rose from 0.667 to 1.0 — more spread, sometimes later.

POS002 (A05): before mean 0.471, after 0.573 — A05 appears later in traces.

POS004 (A07): before mean 0.511, after 0.693 — A07 appears later.

REL items:

REL001 (A01, A03): before co-occurrence 0.275, B_only (A03 only) 0.23; after co-occurrence 0.53, B_only 0. So A03 and A01 now co-occur more.

REL002 (A01, A04): similar — co-occurrence 0.275 → 0.53, B_only 0.23 → 0.

REL003 (A01, A05): before co-occurrence 0.275, B_before_A 0.165 (A05 before A01), neither 0.725; after co-occurrence 0.29, A_only 0.24, neither 0.47, B_before_A 0. Interesting: after, A01 occurs without A05 in 24% of traces; before, A05 occurred before A01 in 16.5%.

REL004 (A01, A06): before co-occurrence 0.275, B_only 0.23, A_before_B 0.165 (A01 before A06); after co-occurrence 0.53, A_before_B 0.13, B_before_A 0.11, interleaved 0.29. So A01 and A06 now co-occur more, in mixed order.

REL005 (A01, A07): before co-occurrence 0.275, B_only 0.23, interleaved 0.275; after co-occurrence 0.29, A_only 0.24, neither 0.47. So before, A07 often occurred without A01 (23%); after, A01 often occurs without A07 (24%).

REL006 (A03, A07): before co-occurrence 0.505; after co-occurrence 0.29, A_only (A03 only) 0.24. So A03 now occurs without A07.

REL007 (A04, A07): same pattern — co-occurrence 0.505 → 0.29, A_only 0.24.

REL008 (A05, A07): before co-occurrence 0.275, B_only (A07 only) 0.23; after co-occurrence 0.29, neither 0.71, A_before_B 0.15. Hmm.

REL009 (A06, A07): before co-occurrence 0.505, B_before_A (A07 before A06) 0.23; after co-occurrence 0.29, A_only 0.24, A_before_B 0.12.

LAG items: many. Let me look at key ones.

LAG003 (A01 then A07 within 5 steps): before, lag 1 dominant (0.285 of ... normalized); after, lag 1 = 0. So before A01 was immediately followed by A07; after that immediate succession disappeared.

LAG009 (A05 then A01): before lag 1 = 0.295; after lag 1 = 0. Before A05 immediately followed by A01; after not.

LAG012 (A07 then A01): before lag 1 = 0; after lag 1 = 0.253. After, A07 immediately followed by A01.

LAG013 (A07 then A05): before lag 1 = 0.256; after lag 1 = 0. Before A07 → A05 immediate; after not.

LAG001 (A01 then A05): before lag 1 = 0; after lag 1 = 0.204. After, A01 immediately followed by A05.

LAG011 (A05 then A07): before lag 1 = 0; after lag 1 = 0.235. After, A05 immediately followed by A07.

LAG010 (A05 then A06): before lag 3 = 0.836; after lag 1 = 0.4375, lag 2 = 0.3125 (support after only 16 — weak).

LAG014 (A07 then A06): before lag 1 = 0.407; after lag 1 = 0.625, lag 2 = 0.375 (support after only 8 — very weak).

LAG004 (A03 then A01): before lags 3-4 dominant; after lags 1-2. LAG006 (A04 then A01): similar. LAG005 (A03 then A07): before lag 1; after lags 4-5. LAG008 (A04 then A07): before lags 1-2; after lags 3-5.

So the picture: In the before window, there was a loop A01 → A07 → {A05, A06} → ... with A05 → A01 closing the loop, and A06 near the end of traces. In the after window, the loop appears re-ordered: A01 → A05 → A07 → A01, with A06 now in the middle of traces and branching to several activities, and A01 also leading to A03/A04/A06.

So the main hypothesis: the order of activities within the repeating block changed — before, A07 came directly after A01 and A05/A06 followed A07; after, A05 comes directly after A01, A07 follows A05, and A07 leads back to A01. Essentially A05 and A07 swapped positions in the loop, or the loop was re-sequenced from A01→A07→A05→A01 to A01→A05→A07→A01.

Let me verify with DIR:

Before:
- A01 → A07 (94%)
- A07 → A05 (43%), A06 (41%), A03 (7%), A04 (8%)
- A05 → A01 (96%)
- A06 → A03 (64%), A04 (36%) [few observations, support 11]

So before loop: A01 → A07 → A05 → A01 (and A07 → A06 → A03/A04).

After:
- A01 → A05 (57%), A06 (18%), A04 (14%), A03 (11%)
- A05 → A07 (91%)
- A07 → A01 (94%)
- A06 → A01 (31%), A03 (28%), A05 (18%), A04 (15%), A07 (8%)

So after loop: A01 → A05 → A07 → A01. And A06 now follows A01 sometimes and leads back to A01/A03/A05.

This is consistent: the sequence A01 → A07 → A05 → A01 became A01 → A05 → A07 → A01. That's a swap of A05 and A07 in the loop, or equivalently A07 moved from directly after A01 to after A05.

Also participation changes: A01 up (27.5% → 53% of traces), A07 down (50.5% → 29%). A06's position moved from end (mean 0.96) to middle (0.48). A06's outgoing support went from 11 to 83 — A06 occurs much more often after (in terms of outgoing transitions). Actually OCC for A06 isn't in the evidence, but DIR005 support 11 → 83 suggests A06 occurs more.

Hmm wait — is this a swap (order/placement change) or a routing change? The evidence shows:

1. Direct successor changes: A01's successor changed from A07 to A05 (DIR001, LAG003 vs LAG001). A05's successor changed from A01 to A07 (DIR004, LAG009 vs LAG011). A07's successor changed from A05/A06 to A01 (DIR006, LAG013/LAG014 vs LAG012).

2. Position changes: A07 later (POS004), A05 later (POS002), A06 from end to middle (POS003).

3. REL changes consistent with co-occurrence changes.

So the hypothesis is about order/placement: A05 and A07 effectively swapped places in the repeating cycle. This needs relational/positional evidence — we have plenty (DIR successor changes, LAG, POS, REL). Direct and consistent.

But there's also a participation change: A01 up, A07 down. Is that part of the same hypothesis or a separate difference? The loop re-sequencing could explain frequency changes partially: if the loop changed, the number of iterations could change. A01 participation doubled (27.5% → 53%), A07 halved (50.5% → 29%). Hmm, that's a participation change on top of the reorder. Actually, if the loop changed from A01→A07→A05→A01 to A01→A05→A07→A01, participation of A01, A05, A07 within the loop should stay the same. The participation changes suggest the loop also executes more often (A01 more) and A07 less. Hmm.

Wait, let me reconsider. Maybe the change is: before, the loop was A01 → A07 → A05 → A01 (with A07 also going to A06 → A03/A04). After, the loop is A01 → A05 → A07 → A01. Additionally, A01 now sometimes goes to A03/A04/A06 directly.

Actually, let me think about what "trace participation" means: share of traces containing the activity. Before: A01 in 27.5% of traces, A07 in 50.5%, A05 in 27.5% (from POS002 support 0.275), A06 in 50.5% (POS003), A03 in ~50.5% (REL006 co-occurrence 0.505 with A07 and A_only 0 → A03 participation 0.505), A04 in ~50.5% (REL007).

After: A01 53%, A07 29%, A05 29%, A06 53%, A03 53% (co-occurrence 0.29 + A_only 0.24), A04 53%.

Interesting: before, A01 and A05 had participation 27.5% while A03, A04, A06, A07 had 50.5%. After, A01, A06 have 53% while A03, A04, A05, A07 have 29%.

REL patterns before: A01 co-occurs with A03/A04/A06/A07 at 0.275, and each of A03/A04/A06/A07 has B_only ≈ 0.23, neither 0.495. So before, when A01 occurs, A03/A04/A06/A07 usually also occur (A01 participation 0.275 = co-occurrence 0.275, A_only 0). But A03/A04/A06/A07 often occur without A01 (0.23).

After: A01 co-occurs with A03/A04/A06 at 0.53 (A_only 0, B_only 0), neither 0.47. So after, A01 and A03/A04/A06 always occur together. A01 with A07: after co-occurrence 0.29, A_only 0.24 — A01 often without A07.

A03 with A07: before co-occurrence 0.505 (always together); after co-occurrence 0.29, A_only 0.24 (A03 without A07).

So before: {A03, A04, A06, A07} formed a group occurring in ~50% of traces, with A01/A05 in ~27.5% of traces (subset). After: {A01, A03, A04, A06} occur together in 53% of traces, with A05/A07 in 29% (subset).

So the group membership changed: A07 moved out of the always-together group and A01 moved in. Hmm, that's a structural change in which activities co-occur.

Let me think of it as: before, traces either contain the block {A03,A04,A06,A07} (50%) or not; within those, half also contain A01,A05. After: traces either contain {A01,A03,A04,A06} (53%) or not; within those, about half contain A05,A07.

Combined with the loop reorder: before loop A01→A07→A05→A01 plus A07→A06→{A03,A04}; after loop A01→A05→A07→A01 plus A01→A06→{A01,A03,A05,A04} and A01→A03/A04.

Hmm, this is getting complex. Let me simplify for the answer.

Main behavioural differences:

1. The direct successors of key activities changed:
   - A01: before, ~94% of its outgoing transitions went to A07; after, ~57% go to A05 and the rest to A06 (~18%), A04 (~14%), A03 (~11%), with no direct A01→A07 observed.
   - A05: before, ~96% to A01; after, ~91% to A07.
   - A07: before, split between A05 (~43%) and A06 (~41%); after, ~94% to A01.

2. Immediate-succession (LAG) evidence matches: A01→A07 within one step before (28% of... actually the LAG components are normalized shares of observed pairs within 5 steps; before lag-1 0.285, after 0). A05→A01 immediate before, gone after. New immediate successions after: A01→A05, A05→A07, A07→A01.

3. Positions: A07 and A05 occur later in traces (mean position ~0.51→0.69 and ~0.47→0.57); A06 moved from near the end (mean ~0.96) to the middle (~0.48).

4. Participation: A01 rose from ~28% to ~53% of traces (mean occurrences 0.53→1.10); A07 fell from ~51% to ~29% (mean 1.03→0.57). A03 and A04 now often occur without A07 (A_only 0.24), whereas before they almost always co-occurred with A07 (0.505).

5. A06: before rarely an origin (11 outgoing transitions) and near trace end; after more frequent (83 outgoing) and mid-trace, branching to A01/A03/A05/A04.

Main hypothesis: the repeating loop was re-sequenced — before, A01 was followed by A07, which led to A05 (or A06), and A05 led back to A01; after, A01 is followed by A05, then A07, which leads back to A01. I.e., A05 and A07 effectively swapped places in the cycle A01 → A07 → A05 → A01 becoming A01 → A05 → A07 → A01. This is an ordering/placement change, directly supported by DIR successor changes and LAG immediate-succession changes, plus POS.

Is this "supported hypothesis" or "weak hypothesis"? The screening shows 35 items vs 0.29 expected — a massive excess, so chance is ruled out as explanation for the ensemble. The relational evidence (DIR + LAG) directly shows the successor changes. Consistency: DIR001, DIR004, DIR006, LAG001/003/009/011/012/013 all agree on the loop reorder. POS agrees. So I'd say "Supported hypothesis" for the re-sequencing.

But wait — there's also the participation change (A01 up, A07 down) and the co-occurrence group change (A03/A04 now without A07). Are these part of the same hypothesis or other differences? The loop reorder doesn't by itself explain participation changes. Actually, hmm — could the participation changes be a consequence? If the loop changed such that A07 became optional or the loop iterates differently... The instructions say: "A change in how often existing paths are taken requires that every activity and path involved is observed in a substantial share of traces in both windows, and that only the shares between alternatives shift; it is not a replacement of one path by another. It does not apply when... a predecessor now leads directly to a successor so that a group of activities is bypassed, or when the number of repetitions per trace changes."

Here A01's mean occurrences per trace more than doubled (0.525 → 1.095) — repetitions changed. And A01 now leads directly to A03/A04/A06 (bypassing?). Actually before, A01 → A07 only; after A01 → A05/A06/A04/A03. So A07 is bypassed sometimes.

So the participation changes are better reported as part of the observed differences but the main hypothesis is the re-sequencing of the loop. Alternatively, the main hypothesis could be "the order of A05 and A07 in the loop swapped" with other differences (participation shifts, A06 repositioning) reported as additional.

Actually, let me reconsider whether the A06 change is part of the main hypothesis. Before: A07 → A06 (41%), A06 → A03/A04, A06 near end of trace. After: A01 → A06 (18%), A06 → A01/A03/A05/A04, A06 mid-trace. So A06 moved from being a follower of A07 near the trace end to being a follower of A01 mid-trace. That's a placement change too. It could be folded into the main hypothesis: the loop was restructured. But to keep the main hypothesis crisp, I'll state the A05/A07 swap as the main hypothesis and mention A06's repositioning either as part of it or under other differences.

Hmm. Let me think about what single hypothesis best explains the most evidence:

Before: cycle C1: A01 → A07 → A05 → A01, with A07 → A06 → {A03, A04} as a side branch, A06 near end.
After: cycle C2: A01 → A05 → A07 → A01, with A01 → A06 → {A01, A03, A05, A04} and A01 → A03/A04 direct branches.

So the hypothesis: within the repeating block, the sequence of A05 and A07 was reversed (A07 before A05 became A05 before A07), and A06 moved from following A07 (near the end) to following A01 (mid-block). Participation also shifted: the block containing A01 now runs in more traces (53% vs 27.5%), while A07 appears in fewer traces (29% vs 51%) — consistent with A07 becoming a later/optional part... hmm, actually A07 participation dropped from 50.5% to 29%, and A01 rose from 27.5% to 53%.

Wait — before, A01 participation 27.5% but A07 50.5%. If the loop A01→A07→A05→A01 ran, all three would co-occur. REL005 (A01, A07) before: co-occurrence 0.275, B_only 0.23 — so A07 occurred without A01 in 23% of traces. So before, there were traces with A07 but no A01 (A07 → A06 → A03/A04 path without the A01 loop?). And after, A01 occurs without A07 (24%) — A01 → A05? No wait, REL003 (A01, A05) after: co-occurrence 0.29, A_only 0.24. So after, A01 occurs without A05 in 24% of traces. And A01 → A06/A04/A03 branches would give A01 without A05 and without A07.

OK the picture is complex but the core finding is robust: the immediate-successor structure among A01, A05, A07 reversed/re-wired.

Now, support level. The screening comparison: 35 items vs 0.29 expected — count many times larger, cannot be explained by chance. Then judge directness/consistency: the DIR and LAG items directly show successor changes; multiple independent-ish indicators (DIR, LAG, POS, REL, OCC) agree. Competing explanations: could this be a rare-variant artifact? With 35 items all pointing the same way and empirical strength ~0.995 for each, chance is implausible. Could the "swap" actually be something else, e.g., a new loop inserted? The evidence can't fully distinguish a swap of A05/A07 from, say, a re-routing where A01 now goes to A05 first. But the direct successor changes are what they are; the hypothesis "the order of A05 and A07 within the cycle reversed" is directly supported by relational evidence.

One caution: LAG/POS use event positions, not clock time — I should note the hypothesis is about order in the trace, not calendar timing. Also, some supports are small (LAG010 after support 16, LAG014 after support 8, DIR005 before support 11) — treat those as weak; I should avoid leaning on them. LAG014 (A07→A06) after support 8 — weak. DIR005 (A06) before support 11 — weak. LAG010 (A05→A06) after support 16 — weakish. I'll base the main hypothesis on the strong items: DIR001, DIR004, DIR006 (supports 105/148, 93/102, 206/113), LAG001, LAG003, LAG009, LAG011, LAG012, LAG013 (supports ~55/58), POS002/003/004, OCC001/002, REL items.

So: Supported hypothesis. The main hypothesis: the execution order of A05 and A07 within the repeating cycle around A01 was reversed: before, A01 led almost exclusively to A07, A07 led mainly to A05 (or A06), and A05 closed the cycle back to A01; after, A01 leads mainly to A05, A05 leads almost exclusively to A07, and A07 leads back to A01. Supporting signs: successor redistribution (DIR001/004/006), immediate-succession flips (LAG003/009/013 gone; LAG001/011/012 new), position shifts (A05, A07 later; POS002/004), participation changes consistent (A01 up, A07 down — though this is arguably a separate difference).
